header.title: DormoVision X™ for Pediatric Sleep Diagnostics
header.subtitle: DormoVision X™ brings diagnostic polysomnography into the home and the lab for patients ages 6+, giving clinicians flexible testing options while keeping acquisition, monitoring, scoring, interpretation, and reporting connected in one workflow.

blocks.heading: The patients you see
blocks.lead: Sleep concerns in children do not always look like sleep problems.

items: Stertor, snoring or noisy breathing during sleep
Suspected obstructive or other sleep-disordered breathing

blocks.heading: Connect symptoms to objective findings
blocks.body: DormoVision X™ ecosystem of products help clinicians relate presenting symptoms and clinical concerns to objective overnight physiology, including EEG-based sleep staging, EOG and EMG, independent nasal and oral airflow, respiratory effort, oxygen saturation, limb movement, and separate head and body position. Type II home PSG and attended Type I in-lab PSG are managed through the same platform, supporting a consistent diagnostic workflow across care settings.

header.title: Why DormoVision X™ for pediatric sleep care?

items.head: Diagnostic PSG in the setting that fits the patient
items.body: DormoVision X™ supports Type II home PSG and attended Type I in-lab PSG, giving clinicians flexibility in where diagnostic evaluation takes place without moving to a separate testing ecosystem.

items.head: Comprehensive PSG with less patient burden
items.body: Wireless, cannula-free recording reduces traditional PSG hardware on the patient and allows Type II PSG to be performed in the child's own sleep environment when appropriate. This may be particularly relevant for children who have difficulty tolerating nasal prongs, extensive wiring, or an overnight lab study.

items.head: Live monitoring, where the study happens
items.body: Technicians can monitor studies and review signal quality in real time during both home and attended in-lab PSG, helping identify signal issues while the recording is still in progress.

items.head: Measuring beyond a single night
items.body: Multi-night home recording gives clinicians the option to collect additional nights when more data is needed, without requiring another overnight lab visit.

items.head: One workflow at home and at the lab
items.body: Home and in-lab studies are managed through the same DormoVision X™ Platform, keeping acquisition, monitoring, scoring, interpretation, and reporting connected across care settings.

blocks.heading: Why this matters
blocks.body: Published pediatric evidence supports both sides of this approach: PSG remains the reference method for objective evaluation when pediatric OSA is suspected, while carefully selected home testing pathways can provide useful diagnostic information outside the lab.

items.head: Alternative tests do not replace PSG
items.body: A systematic review of pediatric OSA diagnostic approaches found limited evidence supporting alternatives to polysomnography, reinforcing the importance of objective physiologic assessment when OSA is suspected.[^1]

items.head: Home testing showed high specificity for clinically significant OSA
items.body: In a prospective pediatric pilot study, home sleep apnea testing demonstrated relatively high specificity for identifying clinically significant OSA in the studied population, supporting carefully selected home testing pathways.[^2]
